The count that made a community. Census 1881 was the first full census of British India (the 1872 attempt was incomplete). It found Muslims roughly 20% overall, a majority in Punjab and about 50% in Bengal, and it told a Bengal weaver and a Punjab landlord that they were one community with one set of interests. Government reports on education, employment and poverty by religion then showed Muslims behind Hindus. Behind in the new jobs. Western education was expensive and most Bengal Muslims were poor ryots. The Ulamas resisted it for fear that Western literature would erode their community control, some wished to preserve Persian, and rich landlords saw little use for middle-class jobs. So Hindus, who took to Western education more readily, gained the new professions. The rulers' plan: appease and divide. The teacher's frame: the goal of imperialism is economic loot and the tool is Divide & Rule, co-opting one side to loot the other. W.W. Hunter's Indian Musalmans (1871) argued the British should appease Muslims, job reservation followed in 1897, and the 1905 Partition made East Bengal and Assam a Muslim Majority Province. All three favoured the elite. Sir Syed's qaums. The Mohammadan Association (1855) was pro-British and opposed the 1857 revolts. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan (1817-98) said India was a summation of qaums and that the Muslim qaum, the former rulers, needed Western education to claim special status; he built MAO College (1875) and the Mohammadan Educational Congress (1886) as a rival to the INC. He was not a full separatist, but he drew the blueprint of the Two Nation Theory. The Hindu wave and the Muslim withdrawal. The Arya Samaj (1875) turned aggressive after Dayanand died in 1883, and the Cow Killing Riots of 1893 followed; the INC, bound by its 1886 rule of political issues only, did not condemn them, and Muslim participation fell. The Hindi-Urdu controversy (success for Hindi in 1900) tied Hindi to Hindus and Urdu to Muslims, and the Swadeshi movement's symbols (Bande Mataram, Kali worship, Ganpati and Shivaji festivals) deepened the alienation. Simla 1906. Elite Muslims led by the Aga Khan met Viceroy Minto 05-10 at Shimla. They asked for no annulment of the Bengal Partition, reservation proportional to population in the ILC, PLCs and jobs, and separate electorates in future council reforms. Separate electorates are the hinge: once Muslims must elect Muslims, the Two Nation Theory is institutionally accepted. The League is born. The All India Muslim League was set up at Dacca in December 1906 to hold the British to the Simla promises, promote Muslim interests and promote Muslim loyalty. Its Green Book was written by Mohsin-ul-Mulk and Mohammed Ali Jauhar, provincial Leagues came in 1907-09, and the London branch (1908) under Ameer Ali influenced ICA 1909. The PCCs became mass instruments only in 1920, so the League had a 13-year head start. Two tracks: repression and reform. Swadeshi (1905-11), the Extremists and Revolutionary Activities (from 1908) made India restless, so the British ran repression and reform together; Morley, a Liberal, was open to reform. Move 1 split the INC: Morley's 1906 Budget speech hinted at council reforms, the Moderates feared Extremist agitation would kill them, and the INC split at Surat in 1907. Move 2 divided Hindus and Muslims through separate electorates. A bigger council, not a stronger one. ICA 1909 made the ILC 69 members (9 + 60: 27 elected, 33 nominated) but kept an official majority, 37 against 32. It used the word 'election' for the first time, with proper indirect elections, gave the PLCs a non-official majority (mostly nominated), put S.P. Sinha in the VEC, and let members vote on Budget items, ask supplementary questions and pass non-binding resolutions. Morley stated there was no intent of responsible government, only Limited Self-Government. The separate electorate. Muslims got separate electorates in the ILC, PLCs and local bodies: 8 of 27 elected ILC seats, about 30% against a population of about 20% (the INC's own 1889 Minority Clause had asked for 20%). They also voted in the general seats, had a lower income threshold and direct elections in Muslim seats. Joint electorates give a candidate of the People; separate ones give a candidate of a Group, for a Group, by a Group. Failure and the long shadow. ICA 1909 lasted only 10 years, the shortest of the council reforms (30, 17, 10, 16, 15). The Moderates wanted real power, the INC's goal since 1906 was Swaraj, Muslims got separate electorates and the legislatures were powerless, so it was a Benevolent Despotism. Minto 05-10 became the Father of Communal Electorate, and organised communal politics, never reversed, hardened until 1947.
